utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. On this Tuesday I wish to greet the accused, the lady and gentlemen attorneys and all the people in and around the courtroom assisting us. We are going to continue the examination-in-chief of the witness. Before that I would like to inform you that we can sit on Thursday morning, which will allow the witness to leave in the afternoon. Therefore, Mr. Registrar, the hearing will be held on Thursday morning and not in the afternoon. Another point. Yesterday, there were certain remarks by Mr. Kovacic on document 1D 01410, and the best thing would be for the translation service of the Tribunal to translate this document once again, to give us a new translation. So, Mr. Registrar, will you ask the CLSS to prepare a new translation. As I said yesterday, it is my impression that Mr. Karnavas has another one hour, 15 minutes, and I see that you're all ready and the pulpit is ready for you to take over.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours. I might have, I might have underestimated the time. I might need a little extra time, of course, taken out of the overall period. I don't think it will be much but we'll move as quickly as we can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Raguz, if I can direct your attention to document P 05051 [Realtime transcript read in error "P 0501"]. We have seen this document in the past in this courtroom, but I just wish to point out one matter. If we look to III, for instance, we see that based on this joint declaration of September 14, 1993, that Dr. Franjo Tudjman has appointed Dr. Mate Boban --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry. According to the record, you have said document P 0501. Would it not rather be P 05051, because that's on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have 5051.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: And it says 051. So, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This document here, if we look at III, we see that Dr. Franjo Tudjman appointed Dr. Mate Granic, the vice-premier, prime minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Croatia and President Alija Izetbegovic appointed Dr. Haris Silajdzic, who was the minister of foreign affairs, pursuant this joint declaration. I believe that yesterday you had indicated that to some extent you were under the understanding that these two individuals were engaged in matters in BiH; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we go to the next document, 1D 01590. 1D 01590. We see this is a protocol from a meeting of the working group for solving humanitarian status and so on. This is from a meeting held in Split on September 25, and we see that Mr. Zubak and Mr. Tadic were on one side with Azra Krajsek, Musan Agovic, and Tarik Jasarevic on the other side, and if we look at very briefly on page 2, items 2, 3 and 4, they talk about working groups. They talk about the preparation for organised voluntary return of relocated displaced persons, and they talk about making progress in the negotiations for the return of refugees. Were you aware of this particular protocol at the time?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And again Mr. Zubak, you'd indicated, was the president of the headquarters, as I understand it, and also he was the vice-president of HVO HZ HB.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Go to the next document, 1D 00928. 928, dated 13 October 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Karnavas. I would only like to ask one question for clarification. Here in the protocol, just in the second part of it on page 1 we find the following paragraph: "Terms defining the territory of the RBiH are," and then, "Territories under control of HVO," and "Territories under control of the army of BiH." My question is the following -- that I understand this definition. On the other hand, I wonder if there were no persons who came from, were expelled from the territory of the Republika Srpska, and I wonder if those persons or those territories had -- should have been taken into account in the work of the respective organs and organisations, so that is why my question is why the territory under the -- in a way, the competence of the Republika Srpska and the army of theirs were not included.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because they were not part of this agreement, nor were they signatories. The war was at its worst at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Yes, of course I agree with your explanation that it was not under the control of either of HVO, nor of the BiH army. My only question related to the fact that there might have been refugees or displaced persons coming from that respective territory, but anyway, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we go on to the next document, which is 1D 00928. We see that this is a report that is directed to Dr. Jadranko Prlic. It's from the Office of Refugees and Displaced Persons, dated 13 October 1993, and of course if we look at the second paragraph it talks about -- it gives numbers. 4.159 displaced persons in total. If we go into the third paragraph we see that it says: "Namely due to Muslim aggression, a large number of Croats were displaced primarily from Travnik, Novi Travnik, Konjic, and Bugojno, and the result of that is that municipalities in these territories organise the reception of a large number of displaced persons." And then we see other statistics as well. And if we go on to the second page, the second paragraph in that page reads: "A convoy for Vares is being organised which would evacuate 4.000 displaced persons from Kakanj and Zenica," and so on. And my question is, Mr. Raguz, were you aware of this report, and if you were, can you please tell us how these numbers, these statistics, came about? Very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with it, but the second paragraph you quoted from, when the reference is to 4.000 displaced persons, and they are just those accommodated in collective centres. There were at the time more than a hundred thousand refugees in the territory under the control of the HVO. Therefore, these indicators were obtained on the basis of reports and requests by people from Vares, Kakanj, and people who represented them. And this situation is something we were familiar with because this exodus of 5.000 Croats from Vares were on the move already for some time. So it was common knowledge at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it if it was common knowledge to you, it would have been common knowledge to UNHCR and others in the international community.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I object to the leading question, Mr. President. He's asking the witness to make an assumption about what someone else knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, it's not leading. It calls for speculation maybe if we're going to be technical about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, then it's objectionable on both grounds, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. I'll rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know whether the international community would have been aware of -- that these people were on the move and, if so, how?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the reports of their offices that they had in the area one can see that they were aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now -- and if we go on to the next document just for -- it's 1D 02373. It's essentially the same document, is it not, only it's addressed to Mr. Zubak? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We move on to the next document, 1D 02183, and we see that this is -- this does not have a -- a date. We see your name at the bottom and it's addressed to Dr. Jadranko Prlic, but perhaps you might be able to assist us. You start by saying: "I wish to advise you that since the joint meeting was held in Medjugorje on 17 October, when at your initiative (at the meeting of the representatives of UNHCR, UNPROFOR, IRC, and EC) the forming of a ... commission for humanitarian aid was initiated ..." and then you end by saying: "Six sessions of the commissions have been held at regular intervals every Tuesday at 1100 hours," and then you go on to talk about that the joint commission establish a method of operation. Could you briefly comment on this? What is this all about?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was the coordinator of the joint commission, and I was informing Dr. Jadranko Prlic in this way about the method of work of the joint commission which was set up, among others, by his own initiative pursuant to the Makarska protocol and in the presence of the representatives of the leading international humanitarian organisations, the UNHCR, the International Committee of the Red Cross, UNPROFOR, and the European Community. As much as it was possible at the time, the flow of humanitarian aid was improved, and you can see that over 120 convoys passed through the area under the control of the HVO unhindered, and this was one of the most effective instruments about which there are written and oral testimony of representatives of all these international organisations. And if I may add, Your Honours, just two more sentences why it is important to note this. Because this area which the HVO has successfully defended was an area through which most of the people had been saved and through which most of the humanitarian aid was delivered. And we must bear in mind that this was a legitimate defensive structure formed when the socialist system was dissolved and the inability of those institutions to protect the whole of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Each convoy was noted regularly, its destination, its location, the amount of humanitarian aid it was carrying, and there were regular records kept of all this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Raguz, and we'll see some of that in due course. If we go on to the next document, 1D 02300, we see that you are addressing Dr. Jadranko Prlic. And if we look at the second page, you talk about -- this is dated 25 November 1993. You say that you are enclosing an official assessment made by the chief of the UNHCR office in Medjugorje, Jerry Hume, about the work of the joint commission. Unfortunately, we don't have -- we don't have the official assessment, so could you -- if you recall, could you please comment on what that official assessment contained?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember it and it must exist in the documents. It is an assessment of the official representative of the UNHCR for the area. He gave a positive assessment, a favourable assessment, and he expressed gratitude and readiness to continue this cooperation, and indeed we established almost daily communication regarding these issues as of then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document is 1D 02179. 1D 02179. I seem to be hearing some whispering. And we can see that this is from the minutes of 4 November 1993, and on the agenda at the very top, discussion on the current situation in Vares. And of course we note under A that there is a problem with evacuation, reception and accommodation of 10.000, 10.000 refugees has to be evenly distributed among all subjects including the municipal HVOs, Croatian Defence Councils. And of course we don't need to go through the entire document, but it would -- is it safe to assume that given that you participated that in this -- in this particular discussion that you would have been aware of the situation in Vares?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now again I ask that question because it has been repeatedly argued by the Prosecution and to some extent by some of those in the international community that the HVO HZ HB, along with others, were engaged in a joint criminal enterprise in part to reverse ethnic cleanse Croat communities in Central Bosnia in order to repopulate parts of Herzegovina to make them more homogenous Croats. So I want to put the question fairly and squarely once again. Were you and others such as Mr. Zubak, Dr. Prlic and others, were you involved in reverse ethnic cleansing? Was this -- was this going on?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday and I repeat, that was absolutely not the case, and here before this Honourable Court I reject any such interpretation of the assistance given to these people. I have to say looking at the documents and preparing for today's hearing I saw some reports not only from the UNHCR but also the European Monitors who monitored the situation on the ground, and at this period of time we had a joint meeting at which I was asked why a thousand people who were accommodated in Kiseljak had not been moved towards Herzegovina. And then they said when I gave my interpretation saying that we wanted these people to stay as long as possible, and they saw this as political reasons, our wish for them to stay there. And they confirmed that the humanitarian conditions did not exist for them to stay. And now when we were acting along humanitarian lines and assisting those people in the way that they were suggesting, then they -- some people interpret this as reverse ethnic cleansing, or a situation when people go to the Republic of Croatia. And they all went, Bosniaks, Croats, Serbs. Then we're accused of wishing to Croatise Istria, for instance, together with the Republic of Croatia. Then when we want to bring them back, they say that we want to make Herzegovina more homogenous. Actually, we were dealing with human suffering and the need to assist them, and that was the sole role of this office, and it was only tasks of that kind that I accepted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Mr. Raguz. Now, just to pick up on that to make sure we all understand, the example that you give about Istria, that's where Croats from Bosnia and Herzegovina, displaced refugees, were put in Pineta; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Pineta.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you go to P 07005 just very quickly. We can see even though I believe that this hasn't been translated, but can you verify for us that this tells us that you have been formally appointed as the head of office, correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] the date is for those of us who can't read Croatian?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was appointed as head of the Office for Refugees and Displaced Persons of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna in Mostar on the 1st of December, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if we look on the right-hand side of the -- of this page, we see Darinko Tadic's name. Could you please tell us what is he being appointed to?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this decision, he was appointed representative of the office in the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. We look at the next document 1D 01432. 1D 01432. We see a letter from Darinko Tadic, and of course you're copied, you're one of the recipients as well as Dr. Jadranko Prlic and the subject is request to register a representative office of the Office for Expelled Persons and Refugees of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, and it does make reference that on 1 December 1993 the government adopted a decision to appoint him as a representative to such an office in the Republic of Croatia. My question is: Why was it necessary to have a representative of your office in Croatia when, in fact, Bosnia and Herzegovina had an embassy in Zagreb, and presumably that embassy was there for everyone from Bosnia and Herzegovina whether they were Serb, Croat, Muslim, or other.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason for this appointment was the large number of refugees in the Republic of Croatia and also the fact that we discussed yesterday when talking of the documents that the office for refugees attached to the embassy of Bosnia and Herzegovina, they frequently had -- were unable to cover the entire refugee population so that a -- a large number of people, refugees, Croats, particularly those in Pineta for whom Croatia renounced this kind of accommodation needed assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. 1D 02170. That's the next document, dated 6 January 1994. This is from Spomenka Cek, but your name is mentioned, and we see that it's -- that it's addressed to Dr. Prlic and it makes reference -- it should be Granic as opposed to Gravanec, Granic and Silajdzic. And we see that in the third paragraph it talks about a joint commission of humanitarian issues will meet on 7 January 1994 in Zagreb attended by Lang, Cek, Raguz, Turkovic, Hurtic, and Maric. Do you know whether this meeting took place and if so what was the purpose of this joint commission meeting?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm sorry. There is no English translation and accordingly no transcript of this answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: My Croatian is getting better.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologises. The microphone was not switched on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you -- could you --

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do I need to repeat?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was present at this meeting, and the meeting was held of the commission for humanitarian affairs. The attendees were those indicated, and this is the implementation of the agreement between Tudjman and Izetbegovic that we saw today and of the meeting held between Granic and Silajdzic two days previously in Vienna. And as a result of their agreement, these joint commissions were formed, and I was a member of this commission for humanitarian affairs. And there were also representatives of the embassy of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the Republic of Croatia, Mr. Turkovic, Hurtic, and Mr. Maric.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. If we go on to the next document, 1D 02182. This is a -- this is dated 31 January 1994. It's addressed to Mr. Valentin Coric, who is now the minister of interior. It's from you and it makes reference to the Wagful-Wakifin Fund Mobile Hospital. Could you please, in one sentence or two, tell us what is this all about?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It concerned a hospital that was transferred or transported in 38 or 40 containers. It was the largest transport of that kind. And as you can see, the destination was the eastern part of Mostar. I signed this request or this authorisation allowing it to go there unhindered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, I'm going to look at three documents in succession because they almost -- they're a packet. Those are the next three documents in your bundle. It's 1D 02024, and then we'll be looking at 1D 02025 and 1D 01855. If we could start with the first document, we see that this is a protocol dated 17 March 1994. Do you see that, sir? In 1D 02024?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if we look at the third document that I made reference to, which is -- the document -- I'm sorry. The next document which is 1D 02025. This is actually the third document. We see it's the same protocol, only if we look at the back, the very last page, we see that there are some signatures with some dates, and we see yours, 9 April 1994; correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: My name hasn't been signed but it's as if it had been. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And you've looked at these two documents, and essentially these two protocols are the same, are they not? One is a draft, the other one being the one that was actually signed?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they're basically identical.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. If we look now to a document -- to document 1D 01855, which is in between the two periods. This is dated 24 March 1994. This is addressed to sector for security, brigadier Marijan Biskic, and here it says: "Enclosed please find the protocol on the passage of humanitarian convoys for your information pursuant to the conclusion of the commission for coordinating relations with UNPROFOR, the EC and the international organisations of 23 March 1994, it is necessary to obtain the opinion of the Ministry of Defence and the chief of the Main Staff of the HVO ... so that the protocol could be finalised and immediately implemented." And my question is: Why would it have been necessary for the Ministry of Defence and the chief of the Main Staff to get involved in this particular protocol?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you follow the way the procedure is laid out, well, each new procedure was more and more precise and increasingly broad because that was necessary. As you have said yourself, as you can see, this was forwarded to them since the war was still raging, and there were certain obligations that military commanders had on the basis of the Geneva Conventions or the Geneva agreement, rather, and this had to do with the fact that they should ensure that humanitarian aid could pass through unhindered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And then later on we'll see some other documents concerning the control of what's in the humanitarian -- each humanitarian convoys, but if I could ask, if you could comment, did there come a time when there appeared to be a problem with some of the contents in these convoys? In other words, contents that were supposedly, you know, for humanitarian purposes when in fact they might have been used or capable of being used for other purposes?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That was a time during which certain reports appeared stating that so-called humanitarian convoys had been abused. So there were twofold possibilities. Either there was an attempt to use so-called humanitarian convoys to transport weapons, or there was intent to transport commercial wares since they were very much needed at the time in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. If we go on to the next document, 1D 01954. We're moving in time, and this is 12 April 1994. This is a protocol from a meeting that was held in Mostar. You've attended it, and this is excerpts, I guess, that were signed by Kreso and Tomic, and of course if we look at the very last paragraph in this -- on the first page it talks about humanitarian organisations are subject to the customs procedure for all types of goods and that such goods are entirely at the free disposal of humanitarian organisations. In any event, without going into detail, what was this meeting about, if you could tell us, and what was happening at or around this particular time?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a meeting of expert groups led by Dr. Sead Kreso on behalf of the government and under the control of the ABiH. That was the government of the republic. And also under Neven Tomic, Mr. Neven Tomic on behalf of Herceg-Bosna. So here you can see that there was cooperation when it came to implementing previously signed agreements, and practical steps were taken in order to solve humanitarian and other issues. Bodies of the HVO and of the HZ HB were always prepared to reach such agreements.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And it talks about -- on the very first paragraph under number 1, it says: "...in accordance with the adopted federal constitution." Is this pre- or post-Washington Agreement that brought the birth of the federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that is later on. I can't exactly see the date. Yes, later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if we look at the next document, 1D 01858, which is connected to the one that we just covered, here we see your name, head of office at the bottom. It makes reference to the protocol from the meeting held on 12 April 1994, and we see that Smajkic is mentioned, and you're mentioned as well. And then we see that there are following conclusions that were adopted where various commissions -- where there's a commission -- a joint commission is established harmonising legal regulations, commence work on the programme, and so on and so forth. And could you tell us a little bit about this? Was this consistent with parts of the obligations for implementing the Washington Agreement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, would you be so kind as to repeat the number of the document because it's not been recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, 1D 01858.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: 1858. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This was an extremely important meeting. Its purpose was to implement the Washington Agreement, and as you can see, I and the minister Mr. Arif Smajkic agreed on the establishment of a joint commission that would continually work on the implementation on this sublaw. It says the fundamental law has been respected, has been laid out on both sides, and it has to be brought into line with the competence of the federation. This is from the constitution of the federation. One should draft a programme, prepare a programme for return. We immediately started working in cooperation with the Bosnian side. We had to have a programme for return and coordinate all humanitarian tasks. This was at the beginning of April 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And I take it that cooperation continued on up until the Dayton Accords?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and it continued when the joint federal ministry for such issues was created. I was elected as the deputy of the minister in that federal ministry that was before Dayton.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And where were you stationed? Where was your office then?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As was the case for the 18 years from Mostar to Sarajevo, we went to Sarajevo, and Dr. Jadranko Prlic and others who were elected to the federal government, we passed through Mount Igman. Peace hadn't been established. We went beneath the airport in Sarajevo. I think we passed through at least on 40 occasions under such conditions and on each occasion it was at risk to life and limb, but we were trying to establish a federation in a joint manner. In good faith.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Only one clarification for Mr. Raguz. The -- your answer in its first sentence you said -- and I believe that it was probably a translation problem, "As was the case for the 18 years from Mostar to Sarajevo, we went to Sarajevo," et cetera, et cetera. So I believe that something is wrong with the translation there. I wonder if you may repeat it again and then the translation will come. That is the first sentence of your answer which in English text, "As was the case for the 18 years from Mostar ..." It doesn't make sense to me at least. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I accept your suggestion that I should be more precise. So up until the ministry was established we travelled to Sarajevo and back, until the entire ministry had in fact been established.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The very last document for this chapter is 1D 02733. And this is -- now again we're moving ahead in time. This is in Vjesnik, 13 May 1995 and you're quoted -- you're quoted as having said, among other things, that more than 15 per cent of Croats have been expelled and you talk about -- that you warn that the census shows that 33 per cent of the displaced persons did not wish to return to their homes even if necessary conditions are created. First of all, have you had a chance to look at this -- to look at this article, and can you give us an indication whether you -- you can confirm what's in it? Maybe some explanations as well.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm this. It was a press conference at which I presented the results of the census of those who had been expelled, displaced, and we carried out this census jointly within the new structure of the federal ministry. These are facts. It's common knowledge in terms of the percentages of expelled and displaced Croats, and this is a situation that we have to confront to this very day and that we have to fight. The statement that 33 per cent of those expelled don't want to return to their homes can be interpreted in the following way: So that means that 67 per cent want to return. That's over two-thirds of that figure. So after the war when people were still very traumatised and given that one knows that in other similar situations at least 40 per cent don't return, well, we can say that these are very precise figures, but we managed to perform the census. We wanted to have precise information concerning the return of people and their desire to return and we worked on the basis of this census.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now I'm going to switch to another topic very quickly. This deals with municipalities. In light of your testimony yesterday and we just wish to give somewhat of a sampling to the Trial Chamber which would further support your testimony, if we look at the first four documents, 1D 02541, 1D 02534, 1D 02532, and 1D 02531, if we could just look at those. You have them in your bundle. They're dated respectively November 25, 1992; 1 February 1993; 1 June 1993; and 29 June 1993. And they deal with Posusje which is that municipality which I understand you even gave us -- you used as an example yesterday; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And have you reviewed these -- these documents, and did they more or less comport with your understanding of what that particular municipality was doing at the time?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If we look at the next set of documents, the three documents 1D 00282, 1D 00300, 1D 0268, and we see that these deal with the municipality of Livno. Again, respectively it's 29 July --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I think that I'm in agreement with some of my colleagues at least that this is not clear. What are you talking about? What -- what -- why Posusje? I don't see Posusje, for instance, in -- mentioned in -- in document 1D 02141. Oh, that's not even one. You go so fast and these documents are in an order which makes it necessary for Judges to go constantly back and forth in this enormous bundle, and we have to look for the documents twice because first we have to look for the number and then we have to look for the English version, which is somewhere unmarked. I really would urge you to do the extra effort to give us the documents in the same order as the witness gets them so that we can follow, because we simply get lost and that is not your interest. You do not want that, and we do not want it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We're trying our very best. I'll slow down, but I think this is a very good example, Judge Trechsel, of how frustrating it must be on my end, because I'm -- I'm labouring under some extreme difficulties with time pressures. I'm not blaming anyone, but this is just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Even more preparations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't wish to belabour the point, Your Honours, however, the electronic system was introduced to be more efficient. In this courtroom we use both. I think it's very useful to use both, and we don't have added resources, and I have lawyers with masters degrees putting these things together. It's very difficult to find staff to do these things. We are working day and night. I -- I wish that I could invite the Trial Chamber to work with us for a week, just for a week to see how it is. I mean, I understand your frustration. We will try to do better next time. I will go slower. I apologise, but with that in mind I'll lead up some extra time just so we can do this. I thought this was a creative way of handling things in a more efficient manner; obviously, I erred. I'll take the blame.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I wish you to be aware of and to agree --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: -- that this is not our personal being offended because we have difficult work. It's in our joint common interest, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I agree but my invitation still stands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we -- we can go back to those documents and we will do one by one. 1D 02541. This is 25 November 1992, and we can see this is -- this deals with consumption of oil for heating school occupied by pupils and a wing of the school and the school gym occupied by refugees. Now, you indicated that Posusje was a rather small municipality, I believe you said 16.000, that was accommodating rather early on large numbers of displaced persons and refugees; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now if you look at the second document which is dated 1 February 1993, and that's 1D 02534, we see that it indicates on paragraph number 2: "Due to the factual situation we ask you to allocate 40.000 litres of oil so as to ease the problem of heating the rooms where the displaced persons and refugees are being accommodated." And this is being addressed to the Office for Displaced Persons, to Darinko Tadic; correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. And here you have indicators for the municipality of Posusje signed by the deputy president of the HVO for the municipality of Posusje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you look at the next document, 1D 02532, here we see again municipality of Posusje at the very top. It's a social enterprise catering in tourism dated 1 June 1993, and it talks about the reception, accommodation and welfare of refugees and displaced persons since 9 April 1992. And of course, it has a breakdown of dinner, laundry, theft of towels and sheets, breakage or theft, and of course, the -- they're asking -- they're asking for this to be covered; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And then if we look at the very last document, 1D 02531, we see again council of Posusje municipality adopted at this particular session on 29 June 1993 part of the miner's hall to accommodate displaced persons. And this was an example based -- you gave us the example of Posusje, and would it be fair to say that this sort of documentation comports with what you were trying to tell us yesterday? Correct? You need --

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say, and correct me if I'm wrong, that just as Posusje municipality was carrying out these activities, other municipalities, as you've testified, were doing the same thing and perhaps even generating the same sorts of documents reflecting their contribution to the issue of refugees and displaced persons?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. There were such contributions and there were at the same time requests for aid.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if we go on to the next set of documents I'm going to be switching on to Livno, Livno municipality. Another example. First document is 1D 00282, dated 29 July 1993. And here we see there is a decision to establish a Municipal Staff for the organisation and coordination of shelter and care for displaced persons and refugees in the territory of the municipality. And were you aware at the time, given your position, that Livno was indeed assisting in their -- in these efforts through this particular Municipal Staff?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. You see on the next document, 1D 00300, the very next day, 30 July 1992, here there is a decision of founding a Municipal Staff for the organisation and coordination of work providing care and welfare to expelled persons and refugees on the territories of the municipalities. Again, this would confirm what you indicated to us earlier, that the municipalities were in charge of carrying out these activities; correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now if we go on to the very last document 1D 00268, which is dated 10 October 1994, here we see there's a decision that's being taken on the cancellation of displaced person status for the citizens of Livno municipality, and it gives the reasons. And again this confirms what you told us yesterday, that it was up to the municipalities to make those sorts of decisions, not just in the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna but also this was based on the legislation carrying out for the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina; correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is correct, but according to the opinion of the municipality and of others, they no longer satisfied the conditions -- or certain individuals no longer satisfied the conditions necessary to have the status of displaced person.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, we are of course all aware that this is outside the time-frame covered by the indictment. Perhaps it will be helpful if you let -- or if you made it understandable why it is still relevant evidence in your opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Yeah. In my opinion it's relevant evidence for a couple of reasons. First and foremost there is a continuation. We're not just dealing 1991 to 1994 in the abstract. As you may recall, the Prosecution began its case in the middle of -- I guess in the Middle Ages talking about who was living where in Bosnia-Herzegovina and they went all the way on to 1997 with I believe it was expert Miller, someone I contest not being an expert but, nonetheless, was indicating that this project, the joint criminal enterprise, continued all the way on to 1997, 1998, because the Croats of Bosnia-Herzegovina, primarily those within the Croatian Community and within the Croatian republic of Herceg-Bosna were against the Dayton Peace Accord and against the constitution as it was framed by Dayton. And we're here -- so we're trying to show a continuity of the events. We've indicated that municipalities played a certain role. Now we're showing it. And it's a role that is continuous. This whole issue concerning displaced persons and refugees is very, very complex, and we're trying to show through some sampling of how the municipalities were dealing with this in conjunction with cooperating with the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, HVO HZ HB, because we can see that there is a coordinating effort but there is not a subordinating -- there's no subordination. We also heard extensively from the internationals and from other witness. The Prosecution's theory is there was this reverse ethnic cleansing and so we're trying to give ample evidence to the Trial Chamber to see the matters in the proper context. It's very difficult. You can't just cut it off at one day. And so that's what the whole purpose of this. We're trying to be as streamline as we possibly can, and so that's -- I don't know if I'm answering your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karnavas. You have answered, and I think in a helpful way. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I have an additional question on the basis of this document regarding Livno. In paragraph 1, there is reference to the citizens of Livno, and it is stated at the end of the paragraph the right to temporary occupation of a flat and financial assistance. Reading this text I asked myself the following question, and I'd like you to clarify it for me: It would appear on the basis of this document that a refugee or displaced person may occupy an apartment and may have financial assistance from the municipality, whichever it may be. In that context, were there cases of people, displaced or refugees, namely in Central Bosnia, who left their village or town, who went to another town or village and without the municipal authority having the time to do anything they occupy an apartment on their own, which may be free or not, saying, "I'm entitled to an apartment because I am a displaced person or a refugee"? Did you have any experience with this type of situation when populations or individuals in large numbers, I'm thinking of Vares, for instance, there were a hundred thousand people leaving Vares and going somewhere else, and who on their own occupy apartments while the municipal authority didn't have time to do anything? Did you come across such situations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. President, there were such situations, but they were in evidence throughout Bosnia and Herzegovina, and we had occasion to see how individual municipalities reacted to such instances. Yesterday, for instance, we saw a document adopted by the Mostar Municipal Council on the removal of people who had illegally moved into an apartment, because unless they had a decision authorising him to move in temporarily, he was staying there illegally, and the municipal authorities had the duty to deal with such situations. Have I managed to answer your question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We're going to go on to another topic. This deals with convoys, this set of documents. Just very briefly the first document is a Prosecution document. We've seen it. We're familiar with it. We don't need too much comment but this is P 10264. If you can just look at it. And we see that this is an agreement on the passage of humanitarian convoys, and my question is: Were you familiar with this particular document?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And that's all that we need to cover at this point. Now, the next document -- and I'm going to look at two documents in succession, but the first one is 1D 01360. This is from the Office for Expelled Persons and Refugees. It's dated 12 October 1993. It's signed by Darinko Tadic, and we see that this -- the subject is approval for unhindered passage. Could you please describe to us what is contained in this document so we have an understanding.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document which pursuant to the Makarska Agreement and confirmed by the group for humanitarian issues establish the procedure and whereby the Office for Expelled Persons and Refugees of Herceg-Bosna was authorised to approve the passage of convoys upon the basis of requests addressed by domestic and international humanitarian organisations. In this request it was necessary for them to indicate the date when the convoy would be leaving, its final destination where the humanitarian aid was being taken, and the registration number of the vehicles, the names of the drivers, and the quantities carried, as this was humanitarian aid and the point was to let it pass unhindered. And on the basis of such a procedure and method of work we managed to achieve excellent results, and each convoy was registered and you can find it in the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If we go on to the next document which is 3D 00921.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wait a moment, please. My colleague has a question, but I also have a question, and I don't know whether the next document may resolve the question, but I give the floor to my colleague. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I see that the document that we have in front of us, D 01360, comes from the Office for Displaced Persons and Refugees authorising unhindered passage of convoys. The question I have for you is whether this was your office that authorised the passage of all humanitarian convoys and whether on the basis of this authorisation your services, your staff members, first examined and inspected all the convoys and to what extent the police or the army intervened with respect to the authorisation of convoys and the security of those convoys.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The office had the authority to grant authorisation only to humanitarian convoys pursuant to the agreements and protocols that we have already seen and analysed. That is the role specified with the approval and agreement of international humanitarian organisations. And this document is an example of the way in which the office granted such authorisation. With this authorisation a humanitarian organisation that is granted permission, and mostly these left from logistic centres at Ploce in Croatia or Split, and there were authorised inspectors envisaged by the protocol who were able to examine the contents. And if the contents were in order, the convoys could set off. And I can tell you that this procedure was respected to the greatest possible degree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Witness. My last question on this subject. I think that you realised and we have even seen in some documents that the parties suspected that there were arms being transported within those humanitarian convoys. Do you have any knowledge of the transportation of non-authorised goods by these convoys on the part of either party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is information and concrete cases when individual smaller, mostly smaller humanitarian organisations which were also active in those areas under those conditions at the time did transport or tried to transport, under the guise of humanitarian aid, other goods, sometimes weapons even.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A brief question, Witness. I come back to the document that we saw a moment ago, 1D 1360. This document dated the 12th of October refers to a convoy of the 15th of October, and my attention was drawn to the destiny of this convoy. It is Zenica, along the route Metkovici, Mali Prolog - I don't know where that is - and destination Zenica. Unless I'm mistaken, in 1993 Zenica was under the control of the ABiH, which would mean that the authorities of Herceg-Bosna are authorising humanitarian convoys with the destination being an area under the control of the ABiH had. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely so, yes. And you will see in the overall review that more than two-thirds of the aid approved by this office in the form of convoys went to areas under the control of the Armija.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. And my last question. To your knowledge, because we have been listening to a great deal about humanitarian convoys, so the Judges are well aware of this problem. I would like to know to the best of your knowledge, did you have within the framework of the activities that you engaged in at the time, did you have knowledge of a humanitarian convoy that you had not authorised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can say with full responsibility that not a single convoy that fulfilled the conditions envisaged by the protocol did not -- was not deprived of permission while he was at the head of this office. So every convoy that fulfilled conditions was allowed to pass.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: If I may add a small question. What was the importance of other convoys that were refused because some condition was not met, according to your office's assessment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Every request that reached the office and was submitted by a humanitarian organisation engaged in these activities was given approval. So we couldn't authorise any other convoys than convoys carrying humanitarian aid. And each humanitarian aid convoy, and I wish to underline in particular that the office never determined where that humanitarian organisation would be taking the convoy, what its destination would be. So we respected their programme and their choice of destination. And there are written reports about this by the head of the UNHCR office - unfortunately, we don't have that document here - and in this document what I'm saying is confirmed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I had understood all that. My question related as it were to the dark side of the moon. Were there requests that had to be rightly, I'm not suggesting anything improper, but were there many, how many requests that for some reason or other had to be rejected?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I shall be able to say more about that when we look at the next document. So I said that there isn't a single request by registered humanitarian organisations that was rejected. There is no concrete evidence of any such case. By now it would have emerged. It's another matter whether some convoys were stopped and whether they had problems en route.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just one point of clarification. You'd indicated that while you were the head of the office, to your knowledge not a single convoy that met the criteria of the protocol was ever denied permission. What about while you were the deputy head of office? Can you recall of any instance when a convoy met all the criteria but your predecessor denied giving access or permission for the convoy?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember any such cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now let's look at the next document, because this covers, I believe, part of your earlier answer. This is 3D 00921. If you could look at it very briefly and then tell us what it is.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document containing a list of all the convoys authorised by the Office for Refugees and Displaced Persons listed according to the date when the approval was given to the humanitarian organisation bringing the humanitarian aid, the destination where the aid was delivered and the quantity of aid carried. And you can see from this that in the period from the 1st of June until the 10th of December, you can see how many convoys there were. Several hundred, I think. And that a total of more than 30.000 tons of humanitarian aid was transported, of which, in answer to your question, Mr. President, there is a summary of how much went to Zenica, Tuzla, East Mostar, Konjic, Jablanica. You will see 25.000 tons of humanitarian aid in total whereas to the area under the HVO, half as much aid went, that is 12.000 tons. So there was no interference with the destination of the aid. That was determined by the humanitarian organisation in question. You can see which they were, the UNHCR, the International Committee of the Red Cross, A.I.C.F., and all the others who contributed to addressing the humanitarian disaster in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right, I have a couple of questions on this just to make sure we have the record correct. If we look at the very first page, we see that the period we're talking about is 1 June to 10 December, 1993; correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if we look at the bottom of the page, we see two different signatures. Is one of those signatures yours?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one on the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And the one on the left, can you recognise it? If not, it doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I gave this document during my testimony, and I signed it. MR, that's me. That's for certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you gave this to the Office of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's when you were -- that's when you were questioned as -- in this case as a suspect?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we look at -- you mentioned some figures. If we just look at the page where you will see the ERN number. There are some numbers at the top right-hand, the one that says 03653938. This figure here, which is 25,847.81, that's dealing with territory that's controlled by the ABiH; correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then if we go to -- again just for the Court's convenience, if we go to the page with the -- the last page of this document, or the second last, I guess it would be, 03653942. We see a figure of 2.315, and that would represent what went to the HVO-controlled territory; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. 12.000. My apologies. Very well. That's all I need for this document. Unless there are other questions, I'm going to move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question for the witness. Looking at this document which we have already examined with other witnesses, so the Chamber's familiar with this document, I am struck by the following conclusion one can make: One has the impression looking at the destination of all these convoys, on the one hand it's Zenica and Sarajevo with other destinations as well, Tuzla and Jablanica, but almost all of these convoys were actually destined to the area under the control of the ABiH, which means intended for Muslims and not Croats. And on the basis of this conclusion, I wonder where are the convoys for the Croats? Were there convoys for the Croats? And then I was looking who was at the origin of these convoys. There's the UNHCR, of course, UNICEF, and then I see certain French non-governmental organisations, how the -- like the Medecins du Monde, the handicapped and so on, and these NGOs were preparing humanitarian convoys not only for Croats but for others as well. Now, as you were in this area of activity, out of 100 convoys, how many went for the Croats and how many for the Muslims? Could you make a breakdown for us?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honour, we have here a record of the convoys, the organisations, and the quantities that went, as we have said, to the area under the control of the ABiH and the area controlled by the HVO, and we can see the concrete figures. 12.505 tons is half the amount that was destined for the areas under control of the Armija, which means that we have precise figures for these area. The area of Zenica also covered Vitez and Novi Travnik. These were areas inhabited by Croats. And then from that central warehouse they were distributed there. We couldn't have precise records of how much of that aid went to the Croats from Zenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My last question. To the best of your knowledge, did you have any information that the Croats had less humanitarian aid than others or the same amount of humanitarian aid or more? Was there discrimination among the final recipients, or is it impossible to provide an answer to that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think both, Your Honour. So it is a fact that individual areas, and these were mostly enclaves, that it was more difficult to reach with the humanitarian aid, and there are indicators that these deliveries of humanitarian aid were very rare there, and this applied to the whole territory, and it's difficult to give you concrete figures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It is a quarter to 4.00. We should normally have a break, and according to the registrar, Mr. Karnavas, you have another 12 minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, but, Your Honours, I'm willing to spend a little bit more time on this -- with this particular witness. It will not affect his departure. I'm told that at least three of my colleagues have no questions, but in light of Judge Trechsel's suggestion, I think that I'm going to need a little bit more time. Again it's going to come -- we'll manage through some other witnesses to cut, but I think the topics that I have for you, just to give you a preview, are reverse ethnic cleansing, statistics, something dealing with the Ljubuski centre, and then a couple of miscellaneous, and some of these documents will indeed cover some of the questions that were asked by the Bench, including the last question, Your Honour, that you have asked Mr. Raguz. So ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber has no objections to this suggestion, but as you are well aware, the other members of the Defence should as a rule have two hours. If some members of the Defence have no questions, well, naturally there's no problem in granting you additional time. I'll consult the other Defence teams. There are three that have no questions. Who has questions? Ms. Nozica, do you have questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it's too early for me to say since the examination-in-chief hasn't been completed yet. If the Stojic Defence has any questions it won't take long, but it's premature for me to decide now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic or Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since I'm on my feet, no, Your Honours, we won't have any questions. It's not necessary. The testimony has been very detailed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have a few brief and simple questions for this witness, but if Mr. Prlic's Defence needs additional time, we will give up those questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Tomasegovic. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honours. As in the case of the Stojic Defence, we'll wait for the completion of the examination-in-chief and then we'll decide. But if we do have any questions it won't take much time. It will be very brief. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ibrisimovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as things stand, at the moment we will have no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. In that case, there are no problems. We'll have a 20-minute break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll now resume.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Raguz, if we could continue now with the next document. It's 1D 02282. And we're going to be discussion three documents in succession concerning this issue, but with respect to this document, if you could look at it. And we see that at the very top it's a note, subject, humanitarian organisation. It's by Colonel Marijan Biskic, and he says: "We enclose herewith intelligence obtained by the Intelligence Administration of the HVO Main Staff about the activities of the serious road trip HO, the humanitarian organisation." Now, if I can look at the next document. I'm going to show you three documents and then I'm going to ask you a question. 1D 02281. 1D 02281. This is from Colonel-General Ante Roso, and this is dated 14 December 1993, where he says -- this is in reference to the reference number. It says: "On the basis of intelligence and our experience so far, some of the material declared as humanitarian has been used exclusively for the needs of the military industry of the Muslim armed forces." And then he goes on to say: "In keeping with the above, remove from convoys the materials under ordinal numbers 1, 5, 6, 7, and 10 in the list attached to this memo ..." and then we see a list. And of course, we flip the page. This is a subject permission for passage of humanitarian convoy, and we see your name at the bottom of it, and, of course, the numbers that were mentioned by General Roso have been circled. And finally, if we look at the last document before I ask you a question. It's 1D 01856. 1D 01856. This is by Marijan Biskic. He's a brigadier at this point and it's regarding humanitarian convoys, and he indicates here: "We have received information that a UNHCR humanitarian convoy which is going into BH army zone of responsibility will besides 34 tons of humanitarian goods also contain 95.000 detonating fuses." So you were asked a question by the Bench earlier whether you had any specific information. Could you please comment on these three documents? What are they about? What's going on?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in light of what I have already said that there were, in fact, such cases, these documents show that this occurred at a certain point in time, and they show which specific humanitarian organisations were concerned. So you have information here from intelligence services, information that shows that humanitarian organisations used humanitarian convoys in such a way. They abused the humanitarian convoys.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we -- we can move on to -- unless there are any questions from the Bench, I'll move on to the next document. 1D 01854. This is a protocol from a meeting held in Posusje on 16 December 1993, chaired by Dr. Jadranko Prlic, and it makes reference to the 17 October 1993 joint meeting held in Medjugorje. We see Granic, Dr. Granic, was there, who was the prime minister of Croatia. And we see that it was agreed, among other things, that a joint commission for humanitarian issues would be formed. And of course, if we look into the second page, we actually see duties and persons in charge of implementing the protocol, and of course, we see that it's the Office of Displaced Persons and Refugees. If we look at the third page under item number 6, it says that the Office of Displaced Persons and Refugees will call meetings of a joint commission, and then under -- under 1, we see your name as a coordinator of the joint commission. And if you could please just tell us very briefly what is this about?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what I can do is confirm once more that this joint commission was in operation. It carried out its tasks adequately and at the meetings of the joint commission all participants and signatories of the protocol were present every week, and representatives of local and international humanitarian organisations also attended. And as you can see in the paragraphs or, rather, the articles of this protocol, there's detailed information on the procedure one had to follow to ensure that humanitarian aid was in fact transported and not other goods. So this just shows how we continued to work in this field in a serous manner, how we continued to coordinate all activities in order to obtain the result that we referred to before the break. I'm referring to the results that relate to the convoys and to the amount of humanitarian aid that was transported.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. If we look on to the next document, 1D 01873. This is dated 20 -- this is a letter by Dr. Jadranko Prlic addressed to General Cot, and it's dated 23 November 1993. Just if we focus our attention on the second paragraph. Dr. Jadranko Prlic is suggesting that Cot's organisation, he's with UNPROFOR at the time, he's in fact, I believe, the head UNPROFOR, to organise an urgent meeting between the highest representatives of the three warring sides in BH in order to bring about peace immediately in all the areas through which the humanitarian aid convoy needs to pass especially in war zones such as Gornji Vakuf. And he talks about his readiness to cooperate in protecting all convoys carrying humanitarian aid. Were you aware at the time of Dr. Jadranko Prlic's efforts, and could you please tell us specifically what, if anything, was happening in the area around Gornji Vakuf around this time?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here we have a specific initiative for the organisation of a meeting of the highest representatives of the three warring sides. The purpose is to establish peace for transport and make it possible for humanitarian aid to pass through. The situation was very delicate, very dangerous. Dr. Prlic referred to that, but unfortunately there were no serious results at that point in time. The period we're dealing with is the 23rd of January, 1993. I don't think there was much of a reaction to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if we go -- if we go on to the next document, 1D 02142, we see this is a letter dated December 7, 1993. It's addressed to Mate Boban, and it's by Dr. Mate Granic, and it makes reference to a convoy called White Passage and another convoy which is to leave for Maglaj, and it has the various routes that have been suggested and, I guess, approved, at least the first one, by Mr. Silajdzic. Were you aware of this -- this particular convoy?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we could look now to the next document 1D 02155, here we find a letter dated December 23, 1993, by Dr. Jadranko Prlic addressed to a Mr. Briquemont wherein Dr. Jadranko Prlic is complaining about the tragic results of the humanitarian action of the White Passage, and he goes on to say that: "The parading of your tanks and transport crews in front of TV cameras only while the convoy was moving across the territory of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna because the journalists and cameras could not stop into the territory under Muslim control misleads again the public around the world that is really not familiar with the activities performed by the UN peace forces in BiH." Then he goes on, and I'll leave it up to the Judges to read the rest. Perhaps they may have some questions on this. But could you -- do you recall why Dr. Jadranko Prlic is complaining about the conduct and behaviour and attitude of UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The case here is a specific one. It was a specific convoy. It was a joint convoy, in fact, a joint humanitarian convoy of a number of humanitarian organisations of both Croatian organisations and Bosniak or Muslim organisations. After a long period of time it was to deliver to the -- to parts of Bosnia and Herzegovina this aid. They had been for three months without any aid. The Croatian government, on the basis of the Granic-Silajdzic agreement, was also in favour of this convoy, and it was UNPROFOR's task to escort the convoy. We can see that serious incidents broke out. I think that there were fatalities, too, when the convoy left the territory under HVO control, and this is what is stated in the letter. The UNPROFOR battalion whose task it was to escort the convoy wasn't appropriately engaged. One has referred to various standards in regard to such issues, and it also mentions the fact that one is prepared for correct relationships at all levels and for cooperation with regard to future humanitarian actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And to your understanding of the events at the time, was Dr. Jadranko Prlic correct in his assessment to Mr. Briquemont?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if we go to the next document, and this is the last one in this chapter. Unless there's questions from the Bench on the previous one, I'll move on to the next. If we go to the next document, P 07669, and it's dated 26 January 1994. If you go to the third page of this document, we see your name and signature as head of the office, and of course, if you could please describe what exactly is the document about, why you're addressing a Dr. Miro Jakovljevic?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I've signed this letter. It was forwarded to the coordinator of these projects for Central Bosnia for the enclaves that were most at risk. In one of those convoys there was the White Path convoy that we have discussed in the previous document. These individuals engaged in the action for Nova Bila and Bosna Srebrena broke through that blockade. They expressed their gratitude. There was support for future actions and we also say that we are in favour of continuing with these joint convoys, Croatian and Bosniak convoys that had as their destination that area that was most at risk.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact if we look at the second page, the last paragraph, you indicate that the most urgent places are Vitez, Busovaca, Novi Travnik, Usora, Zepce, and Kiseljak; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I take it since you authored this document, you would have been aware of the situation in those particular locations hence why you flagged them to this particular individual for urgent need of aid; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. This expresses our desire to continue with activities such as the White Path activities. The places I have mentioned here, Vitez, Busovaca, Novi Travnik, Usora, Zepce, Kiseljak, these are the areas that were a matter of priority. They were under HVO control. But there are also other areas that were under the control of the ABiH at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. We've going to move on to another topic now. Yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me. It would be interesting to know who Dr. Jakovljevic actually was. He's referred to as president, but there are many presidents in the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: There are indeed. There are indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you could tell us who this particular individual is.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was Dr. Miro Jakovljevic. He didn't occupy any political positions and he led a humanitarian action -- project, humanitarian project that was officially called the Humanitarian Paths of Peace and Love for Assistance to Bosnia-Herzegovina. He was a lecturer, a senior lecturer, and it was an extremely successful and humane action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I'd like to follow up on Judge Trechsel's question. Perhaps you could also explain the following to me. In this first paragraph of your letter, at the end of that paragraph you say: "[In English] ...to various parts of Bosnia and Herzegovina on the basis of parity." Parity. [Interpretation] Why parity in relation to Dr. Jakovljevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, these were activities that broke through the humanitarian blockade in force in Central Bosnia. It was successful because it was jointly organised by Croatian and Bosniak humanitarian organisations, and this is why one refers to joint action on the basis of parity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is there a question, Judge Trechsel? Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we go on to the next topic, and this is -- deals with reverse ethnic cleansing. I've broken it into several different areas. The first one deals with Zenica and Kakanj. If we could look at -- I'm going to have you look at four particular documents first and then I'll ask you a question. I'll go slowly. The first document is 1D 02303. This is 15 May 1993. There's no translation I'm told. All right. The next document is 1D 02168. This is 4 October 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me. Mr. Karnavas, you had announced 2303, and then one reads this is 15 May 1993, and then you go to the next document. The previous one, I don't think that it is very informative that this was 15 May 1993. If you want to do something with the document. If you don't, I'm not insisting. It's not my ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I could get you to switch off your microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Let's deal with this. We'll have to spend more time on this. I'll try to thread the needle, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we look at this document, it's addressed to the UNHCR, ECMM, and the Red Cross, and here it's information on the war in Zenica since April 15 of the year, 1993, and have you had a chance to look at this particular document? Please tell us --

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a report containing information on the casualties in the war clash in Zenica, and here you have a record of the casualties, the individuals killed, the facilities destroyed, and this was forwarded to the international organisations. It shows what the situation was in settlements with regard to individuals in certain places. You can see what actually took place in Zenica at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And on the recipient end of the looting and the other sorts of activities that are described, who are they?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, here we can see on the first page that the Croatian Centre was first attacked. That's where the HQ of the Napredak was located, the Catholic Charity Association, the Croatian Central Cultural Association, the Political Prisoners Association, the Croatian Democratic Union, the town gallery. Then there's a list of people whose houses were torched and looted. We have information on the settlements and the names of people who were affected. Most of them were, in fact, Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And were you aware of this activity? Was this information coming your way?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN RAGUZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this information did come our way, although at this time I had not yet been officially appointed, but this information did arrive because, as a rule, I did get involved in such issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, in -- Judge Trechsel, just for the relevancy of this, we're going to go through history and we're going to see that things are developing, which is why we believe there was no reverse ethnic cleansing, hence the reason for going as early as this period.
